methodology_note: Each circle is one county, sized by its total ACS population (not land area, and never touched by the week's change) and positioned as close as possible to its real geographic location without overlapping another circle -- a Dorling cartogram. Position and size are both fixed; only color and height (on the 3D surface below each circle) vary by the week selected above, read from the same weekly hotspot-change data as the main map's own hotspot layer. Stage 1 shows each county's own true shape; stage 2 morphs that shape into its final circle; stage 3 is the rippling surface, with the circles hidden.
